items.en: Gold-leaf soft-serve ice cream
items.section: ソフトクリーム / Soft serve
items.note: Vanilla soft-serve with a sheet of edible gold leaf; the branch's own blog says it stocks no cones or waffle cones at all, so it comes in a cup — the gold itself is inert.

items.en: Plain soft-serve ice cream
items.section: ソフトクリーム / Soft serve
items.note: Dairy soft-serve served in a cup with one plastic spoon; extra spoons for sharing are charged separately, for environmental reasons.

items.en: Soft-serve set over sweet azuki bean paste
items.section: ソフトクリーム / Soft serve
items.note: The branch's popular combination; azuki and rice are fine but the dairy rules out vegan. A pink さくらソフト appears in spring.

items.ja: ドリップコーヒー S
items.en: Drip coffee, small
items.note: Hand-drip coffee from the company's own roastery and one of the cheapest real coffees in the market; black it is gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: Omicho Blend house coffee
items.note: The house blend named for the market itself; also sold as roasted beans to take home.

items.en: Coffee with gold leaf floating on top
items.note: Kanazawa's signature flourish — gold leaf is edible metal, adds nothing but sparkle, and is both gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: Fresh-brewed iced coffee, bottled to order
items.note: Not the carton stuff: the shop grinds a dedicated iced-coffee blend, drips it, flash-chills it and bottles it when you order. Keeps three days.

items.en: Cold-brew (water-drip) coffee
items.note: Slow cold extraction — low acidity, little bitterness; black it is gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: Caffe latte (espresso with steamed milk)
items.note: Dairy milk as standard; ask for the soy version if you need it plant-based. An iced version is also sold.

items.en: Soy latte
items.note: Added by this branch specifically because of vegetarian and overseas customers; one size only (tall), because the soy milk is opened per drink, and limited in quantity.

items.en: Coffee jelly
items.note: Lightly sweetened jellied coffee, made some years from a single origin such as Mandheling Toba Blue; ask whether it is set with gelatin and whether soft-serve goes on top.

items.ja: 自家製シュークリーム
items.en: House-made cream puff
items.note: Choux pastry is wheat flour, egg and butter — not gluten-free and not vegan.

items.en: Coffee yokan — firm sweet-bean jelly block
items.note: Half-dried yokan made with the company's own roasted coffee — azuki, agar and sugar, so normally gluten-free and vegan, and it travels well as a souvenir.

items.en: Seasonal fresh wagashi (one piece)
items.note: Made for Kureha by the famed Yoshihashi confectionery and changed with the season — usually nerikiri (white bean paste + gyuhi rice paste), so normally wheat-free, but ask.

items.en: Whisked matcha with one seasonal wagashi
items.note: The house set and the reason most people come; matcha itself is gluten-free and vegan, the sweet is the unknown.

items.en: Coffee with one seasonal wagashi
items.note: Same sweet as the matcha set, for people who would rather have coffee; black coffee is gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: Matcha-flavoured rice dumplings on a skewer
items.note: Chewy pounded-rice dumplings; rice flour is naturally wheat-free but confirm no soy-sauce glaze.

items.en: Matcha tea and dango served as a set
items.note: Ordering the tea and the dango together is cheaper than ordering them separately.

items.en: Chilled sweet azuki-bean soup with rice dumplings
items.note: Summer dish: cold sweetened red-bean broth over shiratama rice balls; beans and rice only, but confirm the shop's own recipe.

items.en: Chilled kudzu-starch noodles dipped in black-sugar syrup
items.note: Translucent slippery ribbons eaten with kuromitsu; kudzu and sugar contain no wheat, but many shops blend in potato starch — ask.

items.en: Matcha soft-serve ice cream
items.note: Also sold to take away at the front of the machiya; dairy, so not vegan.

items.en: Shaved ice with matcha syrup
items.note: Kureha runs kakigori year-round; toppings such as ice cream or shiratama change the answer, so ask about yours.

items.en: Shaved ice with Kaga roasted-twig-tea syrup
items.note: Bocha is Kanazawa's signature roasted twig tea — nutty rather than sweet, and the local flavour to try here.

items.en: "Grown-up strawberry" shaved ice
items.note: A less-sweet strawberry version made with real fruit rather than bright red syrup.

items.en: Shaved ice with yuzu citrus syrup
items.note: Sharp and citrusy; the lightest of the four ices.

items.en: Shaved ice with matcha syrup and sweet azuki beans
items.note: "Uji kintoki" is the classic combination — green-tea syrup plus a mound of sweetened red beans.

items.en: Green-tea buckwheat noodles
items.note: Cha-soba dough is buckwheat cut with wheat flour, and the dipping broth is bonito dashi with soy sauce.

items.en: Japanese curry over rice
items.note: Japanese curry is thickened with a wheat-flour roux by default.

items.en: Toasted pressed sandwich (fillings vary; matcha-and-azuki in winter)
items.note: Wheat bread; the winter special is thick matcha cream with sweet azuki paste.

items.en: Bowl of ceremonial green tea, frothed with a bamboo chasen
items.note: Stone-ground green tea beaten with hot water — nothing else in the bowl.

items.en: Iced sweetened matcha drink
items.note: In Japan "green tea" on a cafe menu means cold pre-sweetened matcha, not plain tea; ask whether milk goes in.

items.en: Hot coffee
items.note: Black coffee; milk is served on the side.

items.ja: 和三盆アイスカフェオレ
items.en: Iced café au lait sweetened with wasanbon sugar
items.note: Wasanbon is a fine artisanal Japanese cane sugar; the drink contains dairy milk.

items.en: Yuzu citrus cordial
items.note: Fruit and sugar; also offered as ゆずソーダ with soda water.

items.en: Matcha latte
items.note: Matcha with dairy milk; a float version with ice cream is also listed.

items.en: Beer
items.note: Barley beer — a gluten grain.

items.en: Udon in hot broth topped with sweet-simmered fried tofu (abura-age)
items.note: The Kanazawa standard here; wheat udon in a katsuo (bonito) dashi broth.

items.en: Udon in hot broth with assorted vegetable and fishcake toppings
items.note: Kayaku just means 'with the mixed toppings'; wheat noodles, bonito broth.

items.en: Udon in hot broth with tempura — two large prawns plus shimeji and burdock
items.note: A recent diner counted two big prawn tempura, shimeji and gobo tempura in the bowl.

items.en: Soba in hot broth with prawn tempura
items.note: Soba here is wheat-blended and the tempura batter is wheat; current price not confirmed.

items.en: Chilled soba served on a bamboo tray with dipping tsuyu
items.note: Cold noodles you dip; the tsuyu is soy sauce and bonito dashi.

items.en: Soba under sticky toppings — grated yam and similar slippery garnishes
items.note: 'Neba-toro' is the sticky/slimy family of toppings; still wheat-blended noodles in dashi.

items.en: Soba in hot broth topped with a whole sweet-simmered herring
items.note: The herring is simmered in soy sauce, mirin and sugar — a Kansai-style classic.

items.en: Udon in hot broth with a generous pile of wakame seaweed
items.note: Seaweed is the only topping, but the broth is bonito dashi and the noodles are wheat.

items.en: Very thin chilled wheat noodles with dipping sauce (summer)
items.note: Named on the board by a diner as a warm-season item.

items.en: Cold Chinese-style wheat noodles with shredded toppings and a tangy dressing (summer)
items.note: Summer only; wheat ramen noodles and a soy-vinegar dressing.

items.en: Breadcrumbed pork cutlet simmered with onion and egg over rice
items.note: Panko crumb plus a soy-and-dashi simmer — wheat twice over.

items.en: Chicken and egg simmered in sweet dashi over rice
items.note: Reviewers single this out as the house comfort dish; the seasoning is soy sauce, so not GF.

items.en: Oyako-don set — the rice bowl paired with a small udon or soba
items.note: Called the signature lunch set by a regular; an older review quotes ¥630, so expect drift.

items.en: "Samurai residence" sweets plate (assortment of Murakami wagashi with tea)
items.note: The sit-down plate named for the Nagamachi samurai quarter outside the door; contents rotate, so ask what is on it today.

items.ja: わらび餅ドリンク（加賀の国棒ほうじ茶）
items.en: Roasted Kaga twig-tea drink with warabi-mochi jelly cubes at the bottom
items.note: Drink it through a fat straw so you get the bracken-starch mochi; bocha is Kanazawa's signature roasted tea.

items.en: Rice dumplings topped with gold leaf
items.note: Kanazawa produces almost all of Japan's gold leaf; it is inert, tasteless, and both gluten-free and vegan — the dumpling and its glaze are what to ask about.

items.en: Soft pancake folded around mochi and sweet bean paste
items.note: Murakami's best-known sweet; the shop's own allergen line reads wheat, egg, dairy and soy.

items.en: Cube of whole sweet azuki beans in a thin pan-fried batter skin
items.note: The shop lists wheat as the only allergen — the batter skin is flour, so it is out for coeliacs.

items.en: Chewy gyuhi mochi with rich kinako (roasted soy flour) bean paste and sesame
items.note: Shop's allergen line is dairy, soy and sesame — no wheat, but dairy rules it out for vegans.

items.en: Pounded rice mochi wrapped in smooth azuki paste
items.note: Rice and beans; shop's allergen line lists dairy and soy but no wheat.

items.en: Bite-size azuki jelly bar (chestnut or Gorojima sweet-potato)
items.note: Shop declares no allergens at all — beans, sugar and agar; the imo version uses the Kaga heirloom Gorojima kintoki sweet potato.

items.ja: 濃厚でなめらかなチョコ羊羹
items.romaji: Noukou de nameraka na choko youkan
items.en: Rich smooth chocolate yokan jelly bar
items.note: Shop's allergen line is dairy and soy — no wheat, but the milk chocolate means not vegan.

items.en: Wobbly bracken-starch jelly dusted with kinako soy flour
items.note: Made with real hon-warabiko; the only allergen the shop declares is soy (the kinako dusting).

items.en: "Cracked ice" — crystallised sugar-and-agar candy, crisp outside and jelly-soft inside
items.note: Murakami's most photographed sweet and the safest thing in the shop — the allergen line is blank.

items.en: Kaga roasted-twig-tea flavoured cracked-ice candy
items.note: Allergen line blank; the most local of the four flavours (plain, yuzu, bocha, Noto-salt cider).

items.en: Yuzu-citrus cracked-ice candy
items.note: Allergen line blank — sugar, agar and yuzu.

items.en: Red-and-white steamed bun filled with bean paste
items.note: This is the joyo type raised with grated yam — the shop declares yam as the only allergen, no wheat, which is unusual for manju, so double-check.

items.en: Matcha nerikiri sweet with crumbly two-layer bean paste (4 pieces)
items.note: Shop declares no allergens for the matcha version; the yuzu version contains egg.

items.en: Yuzu nerikiri sweet with crumbly two-layer bean paste (4 pieces)
items.note: Hokkaido azuki with an egg-yolk soboro layer — wheat-free but contains egg.

items.en: Small chestnut cake
items.note: Shop lists egg as the only allergen — no wheat declared, but confirm before trusting it for coeliac.

items.en: Baked walnut-and-rice-flour bun filled with chunky azuki paste
items.note: Headline says domestic rice flour, but the shop's own allergen line reads wheat, egg, dairy, walnut and soy — a classic rice-flour trap.

items.en: Pastry parcel of Kaga heirloom sweet-potato paste
items.note: Named for Maeda Toshiie's wife and wrapped in a Kaga-yuzen kimono pattern; house pie dough means wheat, egg and dairy.

items.en: Thin crisp biscuits, 15 to a box
items.note: Wheat and dairy per the shop's allergen line.

items.ja: 和栗のモンブラン大福
items.en: Frozen daifuku mochi filled with Japanese chestnut Mont Blanc cream
items.note: Sold frozen and eaten semi-thawed; allergen line is dairy and egg, no wheat.

items.en: Frozen mugwort-flavoured filled cakes, 6 per pack
items.note: Shop's allergen line reads dairy, soy and sesame with no wheat, which is unusual for anything called oyaki — confirm at the counter.

items.en: Loose single sweets sold by the piece from the counter
items.note: How to buy just one of anything — point and hold up fingers; each type has its own allergens.

items.ja: トースト（ジャム・バター付）
items.en: Thick-cut toast with jam and butter
items.note: Japanese shokupan — wheat bread, plus dairy butter.

items.en: Toast with butter and sweet azuki bean paste
items.note: The kissaten classic: the bean paste is fine, the wheat toast and butter are not.

items.en: Pizza toast — bread with tomato sauce, cheese and toppings
items.note: The house favourite, grilled in an ancient toaster the owner calls her magic oven; still wheat bread and cheese.

items.en: Toast set (toast plus sides and a drink)
items.note: The full breakfast-style plate; wheat bread throughout.

items.en: Beef curry with rice
items.note: Japanese curry sauce is built on a wheat-flour roux — assume gluten unless the shop says otherwise.

items.en: Curry rice topped with a breaded pork cutlet
items.note: Panko breadcrumbs on top of a wheat-roux curry — wheat twice over.

items.en: Shrimp pilaf — buttery savoury rice
items.note: Rice-based so often the least risky plate here, but the butter and the seasoning base (which can include soy sauce or bouillon) need checking.

items.en: Omelette-wrapped ketchup fried rice
items.note: Egg over ketchup-seasoned chicken rice; usually wheat-free, but confirm the sauce and that no demi-glace is poured over.

items.en: Baked shrimp macaroni gratin
items.note: Béchamel is milk thickened with wheat flour, and there is macaroni in it.

items.en: Shrimp doria — rice baked under white sauce and cheese
items.note: Rice underneath, but the white sauce on top is a wheat-flour béchamel.

items.en: Ketchup spaghetti with sausage, onion and green pepper
items.section: パスタ・スパゲッティ
items.note: Japan's own post-war retro pasta, nothing to do with Naples; durum wheat spaghetti.

items.ja: スモールミックスサラダ
items.en: Small mixed green salad
items.note: The one plate here without obvious wheat, but Japanese dressings very often contain soy sauce — ask for it undressed.

items.en: House blend coffee
items.note: The default order; the menu offers a たっぷりビックサイズ (extra-large) pour on any drink for ¥250 more.

items.ja: チャルダ深煎りブレンド
items.en: Cialda dark-roast house blend
items.note: Marked おすすめ (recommended) in red on the menu card — the shop's signature dark roast.

items.en: Charcoal-roasted coffee
items.note: Beans roasted over charcoal — smokier and less acidic than the house blend.

items.en: Vienna coffee — black coffee under whipped cream
items.note: Nothing to do with sausages: 'Wiener' means Viennese. Dairy cream floated on top.

items.en: Café au lait (coffee with hot milk)
items.note: Dairy milk; no plant-milk option is listed on the card.

items.en: Kelp tea — a savoury hot drink of powdered kombu seaweed
items.note: Not kombucha the fermented drink: this is salty seaweed broth. Plant-based, but some commercial kombu-cha powders add wheat-derived starch, so ask.

items.ja: ロイアル・ミルクティー
items.en: Royal milk tea — tea leaves simmered in milk
items.note: Richer than tea-with-milk because the leaves are brewed in the milk itself.

items.en: Iced coffee
items.note: Served unsweetened with syrup and milk on the side, so black is easy to order.

items.en: Melon soda float with ice cream and a cherry
items.note: The photogenic green kissaten icon; this menu's float section specifies a double scoop. Dairy ice cream.

items.en: Iced coffee float with ice cream
items.note: Listed under ※ダブルアイスクリーム入り※ — two scoops go in.

items.en: Hotcakes — thick Japanese pancakes
items.note: Wheat flour, egg and milk; the menu knocks ¥50 off when ordered as a set with any drink.

items.en: Hotcakes topped with sweet azuki bean paste
items.note: Wheat pancakes; the azuki topping is the traditional kissaten flourish.

items.ja: 蜜豆（アイスクリーム入り）
items.en: Mitsumame — agar jelly cubes, beans and fruit in syrup, with ice cream
items.section: アイスクリーム・蜜豆
items.note: The base (kanten agar, azuki, fruit, syrup) is usually wheat-free; the ice cream makes it non-vegan. Plain アイスクリーム is ¥700 and a version served with coffee is ¥1,500.

items.en: Chef's-choice sushi course, about 20–21 pieces — the only thing on offer
items.note: One seating, one menu, no à la carte. The house calls its style 能登前 (Noto-mae) rather than Edomae — Toyama Bay fish landed at Himi and Shinminato, Ishikawa produce, and rice seasoned with red vinegar blended into rice vinegar. Every piece is brushed with soy-based nikiri, so nothing here is gluten-free.

items.en: The day's local fish, whatever came off the boat
items.section: コース内容 (What's in the course)
items.note: Diners report grape shrimp, sweet shrimp, tuna, kohada, tiger prawn and Etchu whelk depending on the month; the chef trained at Tsukiji and in Ginza before opening here in 2016.

items.en: Ingredient surcharge on top of the course price
items.note: The booking pages warn the course price can rise by up to about ¥2,000 depending on what the chef buys that day — budget for it rather than being surprised.

items.en: The house lunch box — the full spread, in a two-tier wooden box
items.note: Fifteen parts: lotus-root steamed cake, three sashimi, mozuku seaweed in vinegar, nanban-marinated fish, dashi omelette, four small bowls, a simmered dish, a grilled dish, tempura, salad, pickles, yuba (tofu-skin) rice, clear soup, dessert and a drink — the tempura batter and the soy seasonings are the wheat.

items.en: 'Flower basket' lunch — a dozen small dishes in a woven basket
items.note: Two sashimi, mozuku, nanban-marinated fish, dashi omelette, a simmered dish, a steamed dish, lotus-root steamed cake, tempura, salad, pickles, rice and miso soup; tempura and soy sauce rule out gluten-free.

items.ja: 能登豚の豚カツランチ
items.en: Noto-pork tonkatsu lunch, coffee and dessert included
items.note: Pork raised on Noto spring water, crumbed and deep-fried, with a simmered dish, tamagoyaki, pickles, rice and miso soup — panko crumb is wheat bread.

items.ja: デザート・ドリンクセット
items.en: Add dessert plus coffee or tea to any dish
items.note: Add-on only — the menu says the dessert set is not sold on its own; ask what the dessert is that day.

items.en: 'Cherry' dinner course — the entry-level kaiseki
items.note: Seasonal multi-course dinner; contents change with the season, and dashi, soy sauce and a deep-fried course run through all of them.

items.en: 'Rin' dinner course — the mid tier
items.note: Same shape as the Sakura course with better materials; flag allergies when booking, since the kitchen sets the menu.

items.en: 'Rabbit' dinner course — the top tier
items.note: The rabbit is the shop's emblem and heads its menus; the top course leans on luxury local fish and Noto beef.

items.ja: 花コース（飲み放題付き）
items.en: 'Flower' course with 90 minutes of all-you-can-drink
items.note: Bookable from four people; the 90-minute drink package is what separates it from the food-only courses.

items.en: Kaga roasted-twig tea, hot or iced
items.note: Kanazawa's signature tea — stems rather than leaves, roasted dark, so it smells toasty and carries almost no bitterness.

items.en: Alcohol-free plum 'wine'
items.note: Sweet plum drink with the alcohol removed; the base varies by brand, so confirm if you avoid grain-derived spirits entirely.

items.en: Chef's seasonal kaiseki, 8–9 courses
items.note: Hassun, an opener, sashimi, a steamed dish, grilled, fried, vinegared, then rice porridge (or green-tea soba) and fruit — you name the budget and the kitchen builds to it; the fried course and the soba are wheat.

items.ja: おまかせ郷土料理の会席
items.en: Chef's KAGA LOCAL kaiseki — the one with jibuni in it
items.note: Same 8–9 course shape but built around Kanazawa's own dishes, with duck jibuni at the centre; this is the course to order if you came to eat Kaga cuisine.

items.en: Duck jibuni — Kanazawa's signature stew
items.section: 郷土料理の会席より (within the local-cuisine course)
items.note: Duck dusted in flour and simmered in soy-dashi with sudare-fu and a dab of wasabi; the flour dusting is exactly why it is not gluten-free, and the fu in it is pure wheat gluten. The shop serves the duck version only in courses from ¥5,500 up.

items.en: Chicken jibuni — the version in the cheapest course
items.section: 郷土料理の会席より (within the local-cuisine course)
items.note: The ¥4,400 course substitutes young chicken for duck; the flour dusting and the wheat-gluten fu are unchanged.

items.ja: 季節のお料理とすっぽんコース
items.romaji: Kisetsu no Oryōri to Suppon Kōsu
items.en: Seasonal dishes plus a whole soft-shell-turtle course
items.note: Raw turtle blood as an aperitif, simmered turtle, sashimi, then turtle hot pot, grilled, fried, vinegared and porridge; the menu writes 丸 ('maru') wherever it means suppon.

items.en: Winter hot-pot course, November to March
items.note: Per person: appetiser, sashimi, your choice of pot — mixed yosenabe, fish chiri, cod, or monkfish — then rice porridge and fruit. The pot broth is soy- and bonito-based.

items.en: Pufferfish course, November to March
items.note: Blanched fugu skin, paper-thin tessa sashimi, the tecchiri hot pot, fugu fried, and porridge to finish — a warmed sake with a toasted fugu fin in it comes with the course.

items.en: Rice porridge, or green-tea soba, as the closing course
items.note: Take the porridge rather than the soba if you avoid wheat — chasoba is buckwheat cut with wheat flour — though either way the broth is soy-and-bonito.

items.en: Udon with chopped sweet fried tofu (abura-age) and spring onion
items.note: The shop calls this its own Kanazawa tradition — chopped abura-age rather than one big sheet.

items.en: The same chopped fried-tofu topping over soba
items.note: Almost every noodle dish here comes as udon or soba — just say which.

items.en: Plain udon in hot dashi broth
items.note: The cheapest way in; Kanazawa udon is deliberately soft, not Sanuki-chewy.

items.en: Plain soba in hot dashi broth
items.note: Wheat-blended buckwheat noodles in a bonito-and-soy broth.

items.en: Udon in hot broth with prawn tempura
items.note: Tempura batter is wheat flour, deep-fried in shared oil.

items.en: Soba in hot broth with prawn tempura
items.note: Same tempura, buckwheat-and-wheat noodles.

items.en: Udon topped with sweet-simmered sliced beef
items.note: The beef is simmered in soy and sugar before it hits the bowl.

items.en: 'Stranger' udon — beef or pork bound with beaten egg
items.note: 'Tanin' (stranger) is the joke opposite of 'oyako' (parent-and-child = chicken and egg).

items.en: Udon with chicken and egg simmered together on top
items.note: Chicken plus egg — the 'parent and child' pairing.

items.en: Curry udon in the shop's own dashi-based roux
items.note: The shop makes the roux from scratch by frying wheat flour with curry powder — three generations of it.

items.ja: クリームソースうどん
items.en: Udon in a rich white cream sauce
items.note: A house original: white sauce with a twist, dairy-based and flour-thickened.

items.en: Udon under a thick starch-glossed broth
items.note: Ankake means the broth is thickened with starch so it stays scalding — the local answer to a cold day.

items.en: Udon in broth with egg drizzled in ribbons through it
items.note: Egg-drop broth; contains egg and bonito dashi.

items.en: Soba topped with a sweet-simmered herring fillet
items.note: Soy-and-sugar simmered herring over wheat-blended soba.

items.en: Soba with grated mountain yam
items.note: Grated yam is vegan itself, but the broth and tsuyu are bonito dashi.

items.en: Soba with grated daikon radish
items.note: Sharp grated daikon cuts the dashi; noodles still wheat-blended.

items.en: Udon with a mixed seafood-and-vegetable stir-fry topping
items.note: Nagasaki-style mixed topping adapted onto the shop's udon.

items.en: Udon simmered and served in its own iron pot
items.note: Arrives boiling in the pot, usually with egg, fishcake and a piece of tempura.

items.en: Udon in a miso-based hotpot broth, served in the pot
items.note: Miso can be barley-based (mugi miso) as well as wheat-inoculated — assume gluten.

items.en: Chilled soba on a bamboo tray with dipping tsuyu (mid-May to mid-Sept)
items.note: The shop's cold menu runs roughly mid-May to mid-September.

items.en: Chinese-style wheat noodles in soup — the old soba shop's other side
items.note: Kanazawa udon shops almost all serve a ramen too; wheat noodles, soy-based soup.

items.en: Ramen with prawn tempura dropped in
items.note: A local oddity worth ordering once — tempura going soft in ramen soup.

items.en: Breadcrumbed pork cutlet with onion and egg over rice (comes with miso soup)
items.note: All the rice bowls come with miso soup.

items.en: Chicken and egg simmered in sweet dashi over rice (comes with miso soup)
items.note: Soy sauce and dashi in the simmer; not GF, not vegan.

items.en: Curry rice with a breadcrumbed pork cutlet on top (salad included)
items.section: カレーライス / Curry rice
items.note: Flour-thickened curry roux plus panko crumb.

items.en: Beef and onion in a sweetish brown sauce over rice (salad included)
items.section: カレーライス / Curry rice
items.note: A house original — plenty of beef and onion, mildly sweet; the roux is flour-based.

items.en: Sweet adzuki bean soup with three rice cakes (mid-Sept to mid-May)
items.note: Beans, sugar and mochi are naturally gluten-free and animal-free, but ask — it is cooked in a wheat kitchen.

items.ja: 土家コーヒー（和菓子付き）
items.en: House blend coffee, a Japanese sweet included
items.note: Also written 土家スペシャルコーヒー; the sweet depends on the day (visitors report chestnut yōkan), and tea is poured as a welcome when you sit down.

items.en: Da Lat coffee — Vietnamese-style, thick and cocoa-bitter
items.note: The owner's own recommendation and unusual for a machiya cafe; he suggests sugar to round out the bitterness, and Vietnamese coffee is normally poured over condensed milk unless you say otherwise.

items.en: Iced coffee
items.note: Black and unsweetened as poured; syrup and milk come on the side.

items.ja: 和三盆アイスコーヒー
items.en: Iced coffee sweetened with wasanbon sugar (summer)
items.note: Wasanbon is a fine-grained artisan sugar from Shikoku with a caramel edge — a summer-only pour here.

items.en: Sweet red-bean soup with mochi (winter)
items.note: Azuki beans simmered with sugar over grilled rice mochi — usually wheat-free and dairy-free, but ask, since the shop has not published ingredients.

items.ja: 金沢おでん 盛り合わせ（5種）
items.en: Kanazawa oden assortment, 5 pieces chosen by the kitchen
items.note: The house dashi is katsuo, kombu and saba-bushi with soy sauce, and the fish-cake pieces carry wheat starch.

items.en: Larger oden assortment, 8 pieces
items.note: Same shared soy-and-bonito pot as the 5-piece set — bigger sampler, not a different broth.

items.en: Wheel of dried wheat gluten simmered in the oden broth
items.note: A Kanazawa oden signature and pure wheat — it is a sponge of gluten that soaks up dashi.

items.en: Whelk (sea snail) simmered whole in the shell, eaten with a pick
items.note: Bonito dashi and soy-sauce broth; the shellfish itself is plain but the pot is not.

items.en: Pink-swirled steamed fish-paste roll, sliced
items.note: Kamaboko-style fish cake — these almost always carry wheat starch as binder.

items.en: Steamed local fish-paste cake, a Kanazawa-only oden piece
items.note: Another surimi cake; assume wheat starch unless the kitchen says otherwise.

items.ja: おばんざい盛り合わせ
items.en: Assorted home-style side dishes on one plate
items.note: One reported plate held salted cod roe simmered, nanban-pickled horse mackerel, som-tam-style dried daikon and potato salad — the line-up rotates.

items.ja: バチバチ油仕上げのよだれ鶏
items.en: "Saliva chicken" — poached chicken thigh finished with sizzling hot oil and chilli-sesame sauce
items.note: The yodare-dori sauce is soy-sauce based, so wheat is in the dressing rather than the chicken.

items.en: Fiery Sichuan-style mapo tofu, numbing with sansho
items.note: Doubanjiang and soy sauce both bring wheat; usually minced pork too, so ask before assuming it is meat-free.

items.ja: 店長自慢の鶏から揚げ（3個・5個）
items.en: The manager's fried chicken, very large pieces, sold in threes or fives
items.note: Kara-age is dredged in wheat flour or potato starch and marinated in soy sauce — treat as wheat.

items.en: Small sandfish, fried then marinated in sweet vinegar with onion
items.note: Fried in a flour dredge and steeped in a soy-vinegar marinade.

items.en: Deep-fried "gasu-ebi", a soft local shrimp too delicate to ship out of Ishikawa
items.note: Battered and shared-fryer fried; a genuinely regional shrimp worth trying if wheat is not an issue.

items.en: Whole rockfish simmered in sweet soy
items.note: "Hachime" is the Hokuriku name for mebaru rockfish; the simmering liquid is soy sauce and mirin.

items.en: Stir-fried leafy greens
items.note: Simple greens, but the wok seasoning is usually soy sauce and the stock may be chicken — ask.

items.en: Fritters wrapped in nori seaweed and deep-fried
items.note: Isobe-age is by definition a wheat-flour batter.

items.en: Crisp-fried prawns in sweet mayonnaise sauce
items.note: Battered prawn, so wheat; mayonnaise means egg as well.

items.en: Tofu topped with sweet-savoury minced-meat miso
items.note: Miso can be barley-based and the meat sauce is usually soy-seasoned.

items.en: Lunch set: the day's oden with rice and soup
items.note: Lunchtime only; the same wheat-containing oden pot as the evening menu.

items.en: Lunch set: ginger-fried pork with rice
items.note: Shogayaki sauce is soy sauce, mirin and ginger — wheat in the sauce.

items.en: Mala tang — build-your-own numbing-spicy soup bowl
items.note: Noodles and the broth base both need checking; most mala broths use soy and some use wheat noodles.

items.ja: No.1 季の美（ジン）× 福岡 八女茶
items.romaji: Ki No Bi (Gin) x Fukuoka Yame-cha
items.en: House speciality tea cocktail: Kyoto Ki No Bi gin cut with Yame green tea
items.section: おすすめドリンク お茶割り
items.note: The shop's own No.1 recommendation; gin and tea only — Ki No Bi is distilled on a rice-spirit base — and they suggest it alongside the oden.

items.ja: No.2 れんと（黒糖焼酎）× 静岡 深蒸し茶
items.en: Amami brown-sugar shochu with deep-steamed Shizuoka green tea
items.section: おすすめドリンク お茶割り
items.note: Kokuto shochu is distilled from sugar cane, so no grain at all.

items.ja: No.5 だいやめ（芋焼酎）× 加賀の紅茶
items.romaji: Daiyame (Imo Shochu) x Kaga no Kocha
items.en: Lychee-scented sweet-potato shochu with Kaga black tea
items.section: おすすめドリンク お茶割り
items.note: Sweet-potato shochu; the shop lists this as the after-dinner one.

items.ja: 特選お茶シリーズ（ポット提供）
items.en: Premium single-origin teas served by the pot, roughly two cups
items.note: Includes Kaga bocha roasted tea, kuromame tea and Kaga black tea — the real non-alcoholic option here.

items.en: Ishikawa plum liqueur, served over ice
items.note: Umeshu is usually distilled-spirit based, but confirm it is not a brewed-grain shochu blend.

items.en: Yuba-and-soba tray set — the house speciality, and the affordable way in
items.note: Tofu skin with soba on a tray with a clear soup; the soba is wheat-blended and the broth is soy-and-bonito, so neither gluten-free nor vegan. Also written 湯葉そば御膳.

items.en: Lunchtime chef's-choice sushi
items.note: The shop posts no menu — this figure comes from diners, so confirm when you book. Third-generation counter, roughly 68 years old, by the Ume bridge on the Asano River.

items.en: Evening chef's-choice sushi
items.note: Reported range, not a posted price. Every piece is brushed with soy-based nikiri; there is no gluten-free version of this meal.

items.en: The day's nigiri, whatever the Sea of Japan gave up
items.note: Recent diners describe spear squid, halfbeak, tuna, sea bream, ark shell, sardine, surf clam, horse mackerel, sweet shrimp, gasu-ebi (a local shrimp too fragile to ship), conger eel and tamago; openers have included cod milt, rock mozuku and sea-cucumber vinegar.

kz_curio_espresso_and_vinta.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Taken from the shop's own menu page (archived); the shop listed them exclusive of consumption tax.

items.ja: バーベキューポークサンド
items.en: Pulled pork sandwich — slow-cooked pork in house barbecue sauce on a bun
items.note: The owners' signature item, made from scratch down to the sauce; add melted cheese or red onion for ¥50 each.

items.ja: ブレックファーストサンド
items.en: Breakfast sandwich — scrambled egg, ham, melted cheese and lettuce on a toasted bun
items.note: Generously sized and served all day; sliced red onion +¥50.

items.en: Veggie sandwich — hummus, garlic-rosemary shiitake, red onion, cucumber, lettuce, feta and yogurt-dill sauce
items.note: Vegetarian but not vegan — feta and yogurt sauce; the bread is wheat.

items.ja: グリークサンドイッチ
items.en: Greek-style sandwich, with seasoned chicken or with chickpeas
items.note: The chickpea version is the closest thing here to vegan — ask whether the sauce contains yogurt.

items.en: Hummus with sliced bread
items.note: The hummus itself (chickpea, tahini, olive oil) is plant-based; it is the bread alongside that carries the wheat.

items.en: Homemade vegetarian chili with melted cheese and red onion
items.note: Meat-free and full of red kidney beans, but it comes topped with cheese — ask them to leave it off.

items.en: Soup of the day
items.note: Changes daily and is written on the blackboard, so ask what is in today's.

items.en: Side of potato chips added to any sandwich
items.note: Bagged chips, so the answer depends on the brand — ask to see the packet.

items.en: Caffè latte — double espresso with steamed milk (latte art on the hot one)
items.note: Soy milk +¥50 makes it vegan; flavoured syrups also +¥50.

items.en: Cappuccino — double espresso under a thick layer of milk foam
items.note: Hot only, per the shop's menu.

items.en: "Zesty mocha" — café mocha finished with fresh orange zest
items.note: The house signature drink; order this if you order nothing else.

items.en: Mexican mocha — cocoa, cinnamon and nutmeg
items.note: Dairy milk as standard; ask for soy (+¥50).

items.en: White Velvet — double espresso with white chocolate and steamed milk
items.note: White chocolate is dairy, so this one cannot be made vegan.

items.en: Cinnamon latte, dusted with cinnamon and cocoa
items.note: Lightly sweetened as standard.

items.en: Americano — espresso let down with hot water; say weak, medium or strong
items.note: The closest thing here to ordinary drip coffee and the safest order for any diet.

items.en: Long black — 180 ml cup, half espresso half hot water; very strong
items.note: Coffee and water only.

items.en: Flat white — 180 ml cup, half espresso half textured milk
items.note: Much stronger than the latte; soy +¥50.

items.ja: エスプレッソ（シングル／ダブル）
items.en: Espresso shot — ristretto (single, sweeter) or lungo (double, more bitter)
items.note: Their own five-bean house blend, each bean roasted to a different level.

items.en: Chai latte — house mix of Assam, Indian spices and fresh ginger with steamed milk
items.note: The chai concentrate is made in-house; soy milk +¥50.

items.en: Matcha latte, lightly sweetened
items.note: Dairy as standard; soy +¥50 makes it vegan.

items.en: Tea — chamomile, rooibos, mint, honey vanilla, Darjeeling, Earl Grey or sencha
items.note: Plain leaf tea; the honey-vanilla blend may contain honey if that matters to you.

items.en: Italian soda — strawberry, watermelon, passionfruit, pineapple, grapefruit or pomegranate
items.note: Add a big spoon of frozen mixed berries for ¥200.

items.ja: エスプレッソアフォガート
items.en: Affogato — double espresso poured over two scoops of vanilla ice cream, walnuts and pumpkin seeds
items.note: Dairy ice cream and nuts on top.

items.ja: ベリーマウンテンデザート
items.en: "Berry Mountain" — warm apple pie under hot mixed berries and vanilla ice cream
items.note: The shop's recommended dessert; pastry base means wheat.

items.ja: 日替わりのペーストリー
items.en: Daily baked pastries — see the blackboard
items.note: Baked in-house and changes daily.

items.en: Aooni IPA — Japanese craft beer, copper, hoppy, full bodied
items.note: Barley beer; Corona and Kirin are ¥700, wine by the glass ¥700.

items.en: Whelk sashimi — raw sea snail, sliced, crunchy and sweet
items.note: Priced strips on the wall put this at the top of the sashimi list; served plain with wasabi, but the soy sauce alongside is wheat.

items.en: Sweet raw shrimp, the Sea of Japan speciality
items.note: Raw and unseasoned; the danger is only the dipping soy.

items.en: Raw squid tossed with fermented soybeans
items.note: Natto's sauce packet is soy-sauce based — ask for it plain if that matters.

items.en: Grated Kaga lotus root steamed to a chewy dumpling under a thick dashi sauce
items.note: This is the Kanazawa classic hasu-mushi; the ankake sauce is dashi and soy and is usually thickened with starch — confirm which.

items.en: Squid pan-fried in butter
items.note: Butter and squid, but soy sauce is the usual finish.

items.en: Squid grilled with just salt
items.note: Salt-grilled rather than sauced, so the closest thing here to a low-wheat order — still confirm the pan.

items.en: Chilled tomato, sliced
items.note: Plain cold tomato — order it undressed and it is genuinely just tomato.

items.en: Squid dressed in sweet vinegared miso
items.note: Nuta miso is often barley miso; ask.

items.en: Sardine dressed in sweet vinegared miso
items.note: Same miso dressing as the squid version.

items.en: Sardine cured in salt and vinegar, served raw-style
items.note: Vinegar-cured, not cooked; the cure itself is usually just salt and vinegar.

items.en: Octopus chopped into rough chunks
items.note: Boiled octopus, plain — soy on the side.

items.en: Cucumber in sweet vinegar
items.note: Sunomono like this often has a splash of dashi in the vinegar, so check for bonito.

items.en: Whole aubergine charred, peeled and chilled
items.note: Normally topped with ginger and bonito flakes and eaten with soy — ask for it bare.

items.en: Daikon radish, simmered for hours until translucent
items.note: Oden pieces here run about ¥80–400. The radish itself is a vegetable, but it sits in a soy-and-bonito pot going back to 1966, so it is neither GF nor vegan.

items.en: Whole boiled egg simmered in the oden broth
items.note: Cooked in the shared wheat-containing broth.

items.en: Wheel of dried wheat gluten, sponged full of dashi
items.note: A recent addition to this counter and the single most wheat-dense thing in the pot.

items.en: Lightly grilled firm tofu, simmered
items.note: Tofu is fine in itself; the broth is not.

items.en: Ginkgo nuts, usually on a skewer
items.note: Faintly bitter, chewy, a very seasonal piece.

items.en: "Bomb" — a sardine tsumine ball packed around ginkgo nuts and a whole boiled egg
items.note: The house showpiece; tsumire binder is normally wheat starch or egg.

items.ja: ロールキャベツ（自家製）
items.en: House-made cabbage rolls simmered in the oden pot
items.note: Minced-meat filling is usually bound with breadcrumbs.

items.ja: 肉団子（自家製・豆腐入り）
items.en: House meatballs lightened with tofu
items.note: Meat-and-tofu balls, another of the owner's own recipes.

items.en: Beef tendon stewed to collagen softness
items.note: Reviewers call this a must-order; the stewing liquid is soy-based.

items.en: House roast pork, cut thick, on a mountain of cabbage
items.note: The regulars' number one. The glaze is a soy marinade, and the cabbage is eaten with the same sauce.

items.en: Female snow crab served in its own shell with both roes
items.note: Kanazawa's icon, legal only from 6 November to late December. The orange uchiko inside and the beady red sotoko outside are the point; a whole one is small enough to eat in a few minutes.

items.en: Thick-cut beef tongue root, salted and grilled medium-rare
items.note: Only the tender tan-moto is used; the rest of the tongue goes into the tendon stew. Salt-grilled, so ask whether any tare touches it.

items.en: Chilled hand-cut soba on a tray with dipping tsuyu
items.note: The plainest way to taste the hand-cut noodles; tsuyu is soy sauce and bonito dashi.

items.en: Soba with grated daikon radish
items.note: Grated daikon and its juice poured over — sharp and cold.

items.en: Chilled soba dipped into tsuyu thickened with grated mountain yam
items.note: The yam makes the dipping sauce cling; still a dashi-and-soy tsuyu.

items.en: Soba under whipped, airy grated mountain yam
items.note: 'Fuwafuwa' means fluffy; the yam is beaten until foamy.

items.en: Soba with grated yam and a raw egg yolk 'moon' on top
items.note: Tsukimi means moon-viewing — the yolk is the moon. Contains raw egg.

items.en: Soba with sliced okra and grated yam
items.note: Two sticky vegetables together; the broth is still bonito dashi.

items.en: Soba with grated daikon 'sleet' and small slippery nameko mushrooms
items.note: 'Mizore' (sleet) describes the look of the grated daikon.

items.en: Soba with small glossy nameko mushrooms
items.note: Nameko come coated in their own natural gel.

items.en: Soba with fermented soybeans
items.note: Strong-smelling sticky fermented soybeans, normally served with a soy-based sauce.

items.en: Soba with a fritter of shredded mixed vegetables
items.note: Kakiage batter is wheat flour and it is deep-fried.

items.en: Soba topped with a sheet of sweet-simmered fried tofu
items.note: 'Kitsune' (fox) because foxes supposedly love abura-age.

items.en: Soba in hot broth with a raw egg cracked on top
items.note: Stir the yolk through the hot broth.

items.en: Chilled udon with a dipping tsuyu
items.note: The udon here is a thin, chewy Komatsu-style noodle rather than a fat one.

items.en: Udon with grated daikon radish
items.note: A recent diner paid ¥968 for this; wheat noodles, bonito tsuyu.

items.en: Udon topped with sweet-simmered fried tofu
items.note: Diners report the udon is a Komatsu-style noodle made with barley as well as wheat — gluten either way.

items.en: Udon with small slippery nameko mushrooms
items.note: Staff often steer you to the udon here even though it is a soba shop.

items.en: Udon with a shredded-vegetable fritter
items.note: Wheat batter, wheat noodles.

items.en: Udon in hot broth with a raw egg on top
items.note: The egg is cracked in raw and cooks in the broth.

items.en: Gold leaf sprinkled over your bowl
items.note: Kanazawa makes almost all of Japan's gold leaf; it is inert and tasteless — pure spectacle.

items.en: Bottled beer, medium bottle
items.note: Beer is malted barley — not gluten-free.

items.en: Local Ishikawa sake, one 180 ml measure
items.note: Sake is rice and koji; usually fine, but ask if any additive worries you.

items.en: Distilled buckwheat shochu
items.note: Distilled from buckwheat; confirm there is no barley in the mash.

items.en: Whisked matcha green tea served with a small Japanese sweet
items.note: The house order, drunk on the red-carpeted veranda facing the garden; the matcha is gluten-free and vegan, but the wagashi that comes with it (reported to be a plain yokan) needs confirming.

items.en: Matcha latte, hot or iced
items.note: Say あたたかい for hot or つめたい for iced; dairy milk.

items.en: Matcha with soda water
items.note: An unusual green fizz — matcha, syrup and soda; vegan as long as no milk or ice cream goes in.

items.en: Matcha ice cream
items.note: The single item priced above the flat ¥500 on the handwritten menu; dairy.

items.en: Coffee
items.note: For anyone who would rather not drink matcha; black it is gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: Black tea
items.note: Ordered plain it is gluten-free and vegan; milk on request makes it neither.

items.en: Hot sweet azuki bean soup
items.note: Reported as a matcha-plus-small-zenzai set; one customer specifically noted 麩 (fu — pure wheat gluten) floating in it, a very Kanazawa touch and a real gluten trap. It is not on the 2024 handwritten menu, so confirm it is still served.

items.en: Shaved ice with syrup
items.note: Summer-only per a 2024 write-up; plain ice and syrup are usually fine, but condensed milk or shiratama rice dumplings on top change that — ask what goes on it.

items.en: House blend coffee
items.note: The master grinds the beans only after you order — the house rule he learned from the Tokyo kissaten master he admired. Black it is gluten-free and vegan.

items.ja: ブレンド（深煎り）おすすめ
items.en: Dark-roast house blend — the shop's recommendation
items.note: Marked おすすめ on the menu; the bean card on the reverse gives it as Toarco Toraja (60%) with Kenya and Brazil.

items.en: Mandheling single origin (Sumatra, Indonesia)
items.note: The shop's own card describes it as thick-bodied and heavy in flavour.

items.en: Toarco Toraja single origin (Sulawesi, Indonesia)
items.note: The card calls it the one straight coffee Key Coffee grows itself — refined acidity, a European favourite.

items.en: Kilimanjaro single origin (Tanzania)
items.note: Promised on the card as acidity as fresh as the blue sky over Kilimanjaro.

items.ja: ヘーゼルナッツカフェ
items.en: Hazelnut-flavoured coffee
items.note: Flavoured coffee — check whether milk or cream is included, and note the nut if you have an allergy.

items.en: Roasted-soybean-flour milk coffee
items.note: A genuine local oddity: kinako (roasted soy flour) whisked into milk coffee, finished with brown sugar if you say yes when the master offers. Kinako is soy, not wheat, but the milk rules out vegan.

items.en: Café au lait
items.note: Dairy milk as standard.

items.ja: アイスコーヒー（一杯ずつ作ります）
items.en: Iced coffee — brewed one cup at a time
items.note: The menu makes a point of it: no pre-made jug, each glass is brewed to order.

items.en: Iced coffee with a scoop of vanilla ice cream
items.note: Dairy ice cream floated on iced coffee.

items.en: 'Jockey coffee' — whisky-spiked iced coffee that looks like a glass of stout
items.note: The menu explains it in a footnote: iced coffee with whisky, poured to resemble dark beer. Whisky is distilled from barley — usually tolerated, but worth flagging if you are strict.

items.en: Black tea, with lemon or with milk
items.note: Say レモン for lemon (vegan) or ミルク for milk (not vegan).

items.ja: ハーブティ（ペパーミント）
items.en: Peppermint herbal tea
items.note: Caffeine-free and, taken plain, both gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: Coffee jelly
items.note: A house speciality the master now serves year-round, having previously put out mame-kanten in winter. Ask whether it is set with gelatin (animal) or agar.

items.ja: 珈琲ゼリー（アイスクリーム入り）
items.en: Coffee jelly with ice cream
items.note: The same jelly with a scoop of dairy ice cream stirred through.

items.en: Beer, small bottle
items.note: Barley malt — straightforwardly not gluten-free.

items.en: Cheesecake
items.note: Cheesecakes in Japan almost always have a wheat-biscuit base or flour in the batter; assume wheat.

items.en: Matcha green tea cake
items.note: Sponge cake — wheat flour, egg and dairy.

items.en: Dense baked chocolate cake
items.note: Some gateau chocolat recipes really are flourless; most Japanese ones still take a spoonful of wheat flour, so ask rather than assume.

items.ja: 無塩完熟トマトジュース
items.en: Unsalted ripe-tomato juice
items.note: The menu specifies salt-free; gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: Kelp tea — a savoury hot drink of powdered kombu seaweed
items.note: Savoury seaweed broth, not a sweet drink. Plant-based, but some kombu-cha powders carry wheat-derived starch.

items.ja: 抹茶（温・冷　米澤茶店、幸の白）
items.romaji: Matcha (Atatakai / Tsumetai — Yonezawa Chaten, Sachi no Shiro)
items.en: Ceremonial matcha, hot or iced, using Yonezawa Tea Shop's 'Sachi no Shiro' grade
items.note: Named tea from a Kanazawa tea merchant, beaten with a bamboo chasen; matcha with water is gluten-free and vegan (抹茶ミルク at ¥600 is neither).

items.en: Buttered toast
items.note: Wheat shokupan, and the cheapest thing on the board. The price was cut off in the menu photo at 「¥35…」, so expect roughly ¥350 rather than treating it as confirmed.

items.ja: チーズトースト（オランダ・ゴーダチーズ）
items.en: Cheese toast made with Dutch Gouda
items.note: The menu names the cheese — real imported Gouda rather than processed slices; still wheat bread. Price cut off in the photo at 「¥55…」, so expect roughly ¥550.

items.ja: 太洋軒の焼き飯（復活した懐かしい昭和の味）
items.en: 'Taiyoken's fried rice' — a revived Showa-era recipe
items.note: The shop's legend: Taiyoken was a packed western-style diner in Korinbo 40 years ago, and the master talked the founder's son into teaching him the recipe on condition it never changed — only he can cook it, so it is off when his wife is on shift. Fried rice normally means soy sauce, so ask. The Kakinokibatake street listing quotes ¥750 with miso soup; the 2025 in-store board reads ¥8xx.

items.en: Omelette-wrapped ketchup fried rice, with miso soup
items.note: Comes with miso soup, which is very often barley miso plus bonito dashi — confirm both if that matters.

items.en: The house invention: oden pieces simmered in Kyoto-duck bone stock instead of the usual dashi
items.note: A chef with a French background runs this pot, so the broth is duck rather than bonito — richer and less soy-forward, but still not vegan and the seasoning needs checking.

items.en: The straight version: kombu, dried shiitake and katsuo dashi, Kyoto-style and gentle
items.note: Bonito in the dashi and soy sauce in the seasoning; order this if you want conventional oden.

items.en: A whole peeled tomato served as an oden piece, hot and sweet-sour
items.note: One of the French-oden items, so it soaks duck stock rather than fish dashi.

items.en: Egg oden, western style — regulars drink the broth it comes in
items.note: Egg, so not vegan; the broth is the question mark.

items.en: Scallop pressed into a hanpen-style fish cake, creamy and dense
items.note: Hanpen is whipped surimi and almost always carries wheat starch or yam binder.

items.en: Sardine ball so soft it will not stay on a skewer, still pink in the middle
items.note: The counter's most-ordered piece; tsumire binder is normally wheat starch.

items.ja: スモークサーモン炙り
items.en: Smoked salmon seared skin-side down, finished with French rock salt
items.note: Salt-finished rather than sauced, which is unusual here — still confirm nothing soy touched the cure.

items.en: The house potato salad
items.note: Japanese potato salad means Kewpie mayonnaise: egg, and often a soy-containing seasoning.

items.ja: トマトと新玉ネギのサラダ
items.en: Tomato and new-season sweet onion salad
items.note: Ask what the dressing is — Japanese house dressings usually carry soy sauce.

items.en: Seared duck breast, sliced thin
items.note: Duck is this kitchen's signature ingredient, the same bird whose bones flavour the French oden.

items.en: Beef tendon stewed until it collapses
items.note: Simmered in soy — a standard izakaya order and a wheat one.

items.ja: クルマ麩のお好み焼風
items.en: Kanazawa's wheel of dried wheat gluten, griddled and dressed like okonomiyaki with sauce and mayonnaise
items.note: Doubly wheat: kuruma-fu is gluten to begin with and okonomiyaki sauce is soy-and-wheat — a clever local twist, and completely off-limits wheat-free.

items.en: Four canapes of spicy pollock roe and mayonnaise on toast
items.note: Bread, plus mentaiko that is usually cured with soy and sake.

items.ja: トマトと生ハムのフライ
items.en: House speciality: tomato and prosciutto breaded and deep-fried
items.note: Marked 名物 (house speciality) on the board. Breadcrumbed and shares the fryer.

items.ja: 地鶏モモ肉のコンフィ
items.en: Free-range chicken thigh cooked slowly in its own fat, French confit style
items.note: Confit is meat, fat and salt; the seasoning and any sauce are what to ask about.

items.en: Three whole green-eye fish, breaded and fried, eaten bones and all
items.note: Mehikari is a small deep-water fish with huge glowing eyes; breadcrumbed.

items.ja: 揚げたてポテトチーズ
items.en: Hot fried potato with melting cheese
items.note: Potato and dairy, but the fryer is shared with breadcrumbed items.

items.en: Breaded fried oysters

items.en: Half an avocado warmed through in the oden broth
items.note: One of the shop's oddities and photographed constantly; the flesh turns custardy in hot stock.

items.en: Cod milt simmered in the oden pot — winter only

items.en: Cabbage roll simmered in the oden broth

items.en: Oysters floured and pan-fried in butter, French style

items.en: Draught beer

kz_zenrin_cafe.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The cafe publishes a monthly PDF of events but no food menu, so these come from visitor reports and prices have risen steadily (the curry was ¥450 in 2012, ¥550 in 2019).

items.en: "Tanto" curry rice — the house European-style curry, served with a small salad
items.note: The one thing this cafe is known for: creamy rather than fiery, heated by Hakusan kensaki-nanba chilli and seasoned with local Naoyoshi soy sauce — so wheat is in both the roux and the soy.

items.en: Fried chicken added on top of the curry
items.note: Karaage is marinated in soy sauce and dusted in flour or potato starch before frying.

items.en: Coffee
items.note: Black coffee; this is a welfare-run community cafe, so the drinks are deliberately cheap.

items.ja: ロイヤルミルクティー
items.en: Royal milk tea — tea simmered in milk
items.note: Made with dairy milk rather than a splash added at the table.

items.en: House blend coffee
items.note: Under ¥500 — this is a working person's kissaten behind Kanazawa Station, not a tourist one. Black it is gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: 'American' coffee — a lighter, weaker brew
items.note: In Japan this means a thinner extraction, not filter-versus-espresso.

items.en: Vienna coffee — black coffee under whipped cream
items.note: Not sausage coffee: 'Wiener' means Viennese. Dairy cream on top, stirred in as it melts.

items.en: Café au lait
items.note: Half coffee, half hot dairy milk.

items.en: Hot cocoa topped with whipped cream
items.note: Cocoa mixes sometimes carry wheat-derived starch; the cream is dairy either way.

items.en: Black tea
items.note: Plain, it is gluten-free and vegan.

items.ja: ロイヤルミルクティー
items.en: Royal milk tea — leaves simmered in milk
items.note: Brewed in the milk rather than milk added afterwards; dairy.

items.en: Matcha latte
items.note: Sweetened matcha with dairy milk.

items.en: Kelp tea — a savoury hot drink of powdered kombu seaweed
items.note: Salty rather than sweet, and a common non-coffee order for older regulars; plant-based, but check the powder for wheat starch.

items.en: Iced coffee
items.note: Syrup and milk usually arrive on the side, so black is easy to order.

items.ja: ウインナーアイスコーヒー
items.en: Iced coffee under whipped cream
items.note: The cold version of the Vienna; dairy cream.

items.en: Lemon squash made with fresh-squeezed lemon
items.note: The 生 means real fruit rather than cordial — lemon juice, syrup and soda; gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: Matcha milkshake
items.note: Shaken matcha, milk and usually egg — a retro kissaten shake, not a modern frappe.

items.en: Milkshake — milk, egg yolk and sugar, whipped
items.note: The Japanese version traditionally contains raw egg as well as milk.

items.en: Iced coffee with a scoop of ice cream
items.note: Dairy ice cream.

items.en: Melon soda float with ice cream
items.note: The green kissaten classic; order ソーダ水 (¥500) instead if you want the same fizz without the scoop.

items.ja: カレーライス（サラダ付）
items.en: Curry rice, with a side salad
items.note: Japanese curry sauce is thickened with a wheat-flour roux — the standard gluten trap on any kissaten menu.

items.ja: 五目チャーハン（サラダ・スープ付）
items.en: Five-ingredient Chinese-style fried rice, with salad and soup
items.note: Rice-based, but fried rice is almost always finished with soy sauce (wheat) — ask before assuming.

items.ja: 海老ピラフ（サラダ・スープ付）
items.en: Shrimp pilaf, with salad and soup
items.note: Buttery savoury rice; both the seasoning base and the soup that comes with it need checking.

items.ja: 親子丼（味噌汁・漬物付）
items.en: Chicken and egg simmered over rice, with miso soup and pickles
items.note: The name means 'parent and child' — chicken and egg. The simmering liquid is soy sauce, mirin and bonito dashi, so wheat and fish are both in it.

items.en: Simmered beef over rice, with miso soup and pickles
items.note: Beef and onion simmered in soy sauce and dashi — wheat in the soy sauce.

items.ja: スパゲッティ ミートソース（サラダ付）
items.en: Spaghetti bolognese, with a side salad
items.note: Wheat pasta. Order any お食事 dish between 11:30 and 13:00 on a weekday and coffee is ¥200.

items.ja: スパゲッティ メンタイソース（スープ付）
items.en: Spaghetti in spicy pollock-roe sauce, with soup
items.note: Mentaiko is chilli-marinated pollock roe, a Japanese pasta staple; wheat pasta plus fish roe.

items.ja: トースト（バターor ジャム）
items.en: Toast with either butter or jam
items.note: Pick one spread; both together is ¥550. Wheat bread.

items.ja: ハムトースト（ハム、レタス、トマト入り）
items.en: Ham toast with lettuce and tomato
items.note: Essentially a hot ham sandwich; ¥800 with soup. Wheat bread.

items.en: Keema (minced meat) curry with rice, salad, and coffee or tea
items.note: Full of green peas and only gently spiced — an old-fashioned kissaten curry, mildly sweet; wheat roux.

items.en: Hayashi rice — beef and onion in a rich tomato-demiglace sauce over rice
items.note: Comes with salad; demiglace is built on a wheat-flour roux.

items.en: Chicken curry with rice
items.note: The third of the shop's rice plates; lunch service runs roughly 11:30–14:00 at a discount.

items.en: Toast set — thick buttered toast with a drink
items.note: The morning order in any Japanese kissaten.

items.en: Cake set — a slice of the day's cake with coffee or tea
items.note: Tea comes in a pot with about two cups' worth; the cake changes, so look in the case.

items.ja: グラノーラのチーズケーキ
items.en: Layered cheesecake on a granola base
items.note: The house favourite — multi-layered and gently flavoured; usually ordered as the ¥700 cake set.

items.ja: 黒蜜きなこのロールケーキ
items.en: Roll cake with black-sugar syrup and roasted soy flour
items.note: Aromatic kinako with unsweetened whipped cream; sponge cake, so wheat and egg.

items.en: Apple tart
items.note: One of the rotating cake-set choices.

items.en: Hot coffee
items.note: Black; drunk under a Chagall print and 1930s stained glass in a registered cultural-property building.

items.en: Iced coffee
items.note: Comes unsweetened with syrup and milk on the side.

items.en: Black tea, served in a pot
items.note: About two cups per pot; milk on request makes it non-vegan.

items.en: Cream soda — green melon soda topped with a scoop of vanilla ice cream
items.note: The signature retro-kissaten drink; dairy ice cream on top.

items.en: Guinness Draught
items.note: The cafe turns into a bar in the evening (open to 22:00); Guinness is a barley stout.

items.en: Buttered toast
items.note: Item 1 on a fully numbered menu — you can simply point at the number. Wheat bread.

items.en: Sandwich
items.note: Crustless white-bread sandwich, kissaten style — usually ham, egg or tuna with mayonnaise.

items.en: Ham on toast
items.note: Wheat bread plus cured pork.

items.en: Egg toast
items.note: Egg — usually egg salad or a fried egg — on toast.

items.en: Pizza toast — tomato sauce and cheese grilled on bread
items.note: The 1960s Japanese answer to pizza; wheat bread and cheese.

items.en: Stir-fried thick wheat noodles
items.note: Udon is wheat and it is fried with soy sauce — wheat twice over.

items.en: Stir-fried noodles in sweet-savoury brown sauce
items.note: Despite 'soba' in the name these are wheat noodles, and the sauce is wheat-based too.

items.en: Spaghetti, tomato/ketchup style
items.note: Wheat pasta.

items.ja: ホワイトスパゲッティ
items.en: 'White' spaghetti — cream-sauce pasta
items.note: The white sauce is a milk-and-wheat-flour béchamel on top of wheat pasta.

items.en: Ramen — choose miso, soy sauce or salt broth
items.note: Ramen noodles are wheat, and even the 'salt' broth is normally built on pork or chicken stock. Say みそ / しょうゆ / しお to pick.

items.en: Chilled very fine white noodles with dipping broth
items.note: Somen are hair-thin wheat noodles, and the tsuyu dip is soy sauce plus bonito dashi.

items.en: Udon noodles in hot broth
items.note: The cheapest hot meal on the board; wheat noodles in a dashi-and-soy broth.

items.en: Japanese curry rice
items.note: Roux-thickened Japanese curry — wheat flour is exactly what makes it thick.

items.en: Baked curry — curry rice topped with cheese and browned in the oven
items.note: The most expensive plate here and the one regulars order; still a wheat-roux curry.

items.en: 'White curry' — pale cream-based curry
items.note: An unusual novelty: curry built on a white cream sauce instead of the brown roux — but it is still a flour-thickened sauce. Price digits were cut off in the menu photo.

items.en: Simmered beef and onion over rice
items.note: Simmered in soy sauce and dashi.

items.en: Fried rice
items.note: The same dish as chahan; almost always seasoned with soy sauce, so ask before treating it as wheat-free.

items.en: Omelette over ketchup fried rice
items.note: Egg and rice; the ketchup rice is usually wheat-free but confirm there is no soy sauce or demi-glace.

items.en: Rice balls
items.note: Plain salted rice is fine, but the filling decides it — pickled plum is vegan and wheat-free, tuna-mayo and salmon are neither.

items.en: Rice with tiny dried whitebait
items.note: Chirimen-jako are miniature dried sardines stirred through hot rice — fish, so never vegan; check whether soy sauce is added. Price digits were cut off in the menu photo.

items.en: Coffee
items.note: Drink number 1 on the list; black it is gluten-free and vegan.

items.en: Black tea
items.note: Plain black tea, gluten-free and vegan as served.

items.en: Morning set — served until 10 a.m.
items.note: The Japanese morning-set ritual: a drink arrives with toast and usually a boiled egg. Toast means wheat.

items.en: Melon soda float with ice cream
items.note: Plain ソーダ (¥450) without the scoop is the vegan version.

items.en: Iced milk tea
items.note: Dairy milk; plain アイスティー (¥600) is the vegan choice.

items.en: Top-grade seafood bowl — the loaded one
items.note: Blackthroat seaperch, tuna, white shrimp, salmon roe, octopus, sea bream, sweet shrimp, squid, salmon, crab claw and steamed prawn over sushi rice; the dish of soy sauce beside it is wheat, so bring tamari if that matters.

items.en: Omicho seafood bowl — the middle option
items.note: The standard market bowl: an assortment of the day's sashimi over rice.

items.en: Market's-choice bowl — the value pick
items.note: Cheapest full-size bowl; the kitchen chooses the toppings from whatever is good that morning.

items.en: Blackthroat seaperch bowl
items.note: Nodoguro is the luxury fish of the Sea of Japan — so fatty it is often called 'white toro'; usually lightly seared before it goes on the rice.

items.en: Salmon-roe bowl
items.note: Roe is cured in soy sauce and sake before serving, which is where the wheat comes in.

items.en: Tuna bowl
items.note: All tuna, no mixed toppings — for people who want one fish done properly.

items.en: Winter yellowtail bowl
items.note: Kanburi is the cold-season yellowtail of Toyama Bay, at its fattiest from December to February — a Hokuriku winter marker.

items.en: Salmon bowl
items.note: The safe order if the rest of the counter looks intimidating.

items.en: Kids' seafood bowl
items.note: Half-size, mild toppings; the shop makes a point of catering to children and to people who dislike raw fish.

items.en: Kids' udon
items.note: Udon noodles are wheat and the broth is soy-and-bonito.

items.en: Five-kind sashimi plate
items.note: Plain sliced fish is the closest thing here to gluten-free — the soy sauce is the problem, not the fish.

items.en: Kanazawa-style oden, simmered in bonito dashi
items.note: The shop's own draw beside the bowls; the popular pieces are the broth-soaked daikon and the kuruma-fu — a wheel of pure wheat gluten that is the signature of Kanazawa oden. The pot is soy-and-bonito, so even the daikon is not gluten-free or vegan.

items.en: Oden set meal with rice
items.note: Oden with rice and soup; no price published, and the shop runs day-only discounts posted on the shopfront.

items.en: Noto rock mozuku seaweed, in vinegar
items.note: Fine, slippery seaweed served cold in a vinegar dressing — the dressing usually contains dashi and soy, so ask.

items.ja: 富山のホタルイカ沖漬
items.en: Toyama firefly squid cured in soy
items.note: Thumb-sized squid that glow blue in Toyama Bay each spring, cured whole in soy sauce and eaten in one bite — intense, and definitively wheat because of the cure.

items.en: Medium mug of draught beer
items.note: Beer is barley — the shop also carries Ishikawa sake such as Tengumai, Kikuhime and Fukumasamune.

items.en: 'Million-koku' bowl — the flagship, named for the Kaga domain
