items.note: The house's loaded bowl — reviewers describe nodoguro, botan-ebi and sea urchin on it. Amatsubo took over the old じもの亭 site in Omicho in February 2025, so this is their branch menu, not the previous owner's; the prices below come from the group's own listing and recent diners report some bowls running a few hundred yen higher.

items.en: Omicho seafood bowl — the standard mixed bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Assorted sashimi over sushi rice; the soy sauce served with it is wheat-brewed.

items.en: Small seafood bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Half-size — the sensible order if you plan to graze the rest of the market.

items.en: Sweet shrimp bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Ama-ebi are the small translucent shrimp of the Sea of Japan, eaten raw and genuinely sweet — a Kanazawa staple.

items.en: Shrimp and crab bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Ask whether the crab is real leg meat or surimi stick — surimi (kanikama) contains wheat starch.

items.en: 'Sea of Japan' seafood bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: A wider assortment than the standard bowl, weighted to local catch.

items.en: Tuna bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Lean tuna only, sliced over rice — 'tekka' is the old gambling-den name for it.

items.en: Salmon and salmon-roe bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Parent and child in one bowl; the roe is soy-cured, so wheat.

items.en: Tuna and squid bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Two toppings, half and half.

items.en: Salmon-roe bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: A solid blanket of roe; each bead pops with soy-cured brine.

items.en: Sea urchin bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: The priciest single-topping bowl; urchin is sold by grade, so ask what it is that day.

items.en: Three-colour bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Three premium toppings laid in stripes — usually urchin, roe and crab or tuna.

items.en: Sea urchin and salmon-roe bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: The two luxury toppings side by side.

items.en: Crab bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Ishikawa's snow crab is branded 加能ガニ (male) and 香箱ガニ (female, roe-filled, 6 Nov to late December only) — worth asking which crab is in the bowl.

items.en: Crab and salmon-roe bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Crab meat with a band of roe over it.

items.en: Prawn tempura bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: The cooked option if raw fish is not for you — but tempura batter is wheat flour and the tare is soy.

items.en: Grilled eel bowl
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: Eel lacquered with a sweet soy tare over rice; the tare is the wheat.

items.en: Wagyu steak box
items.section: 近江町市場店 丼メニュー (Omicho branch bowls)
items.note: The one land-animal main on the branch menu; steak sauce is soy-based.

items.en: The house oden, priced per piece
items.note: Pick from a long list — egg, daikon, konnyaku, thick fried tofu, chikuwa, satsuma-age, the pink-swirled akamaki, mochi pouches, whelk, rolled yuba and kuruma-fu. The fu is pure wheat gluten and the fish cakes are bound with wheat starch; the pot itself is soy-and-bonito.

items.en: Grilled eel, glazed
items.note: Live eel split, skewered, charcoal-grilled and dipped again and again in a tare the family makes on site. The shop's own blog prices a whole grilled eel at ¥3,800–¥5,300 depending on its weight, and quoted 「うなぎ蒲焼き 4,000円から」 in December 2025. The tare is soy sauce and mirin, so it is wheat. Sold by the piece over the counter, not as a sit-down meal.

items.en: Eel grilled plain, no sauce
items.note: The unglazed version — salt and smoke only, so it is the one eel preparation that avoids the soy tare; still ask, as the same grill and brush are used for kabayaki.

items.en: Grilled loach, glazed — the shop's rarity
items.note: Wild domestic loach, a small muddy-river fish grilled whole on a skewer — ¥150 each, so the cheap, strange thing to try. The shop's blog says it routinely sells out by 11am. Same soy tare, same wheat.

items.en: Eel rolled in omelette
items.note: Glazed eel wrapped in a rolled egg omelette — the omelette is usually seasoned with mirin and soy.

items.en: Eel over rice in a lacquer box
items.note: The takeaway box version; no price is published anywhere, and the family is upfront that they are not the cheapest stall in the market.

items.en: Snow crab (the larger, meatier one), boiled in-store
items.note: 加能ガニ is Ishikawa's brand name for the male snow crab; they boil it themselves in natural salt and purified water. Plain boiled crab has no wheat in it — the dipping vinegar might.

items.en: Roe-filled snow crab, served in its own shell
items.note: The Kanazawa obsession: a small roe-bearing snow crab packed back into its shell with the orange outer roe and the darker inner roe. Legal season is roughly 6 November to late December only — the shop simply stops selling crab when the local catch ends.

items.en: Horsehair crab (spring only)
items.note: Sold in spring when the local ones come in; prized for the miso (the brown paste inside the shell) rather than the leg meat.

items.ja: 甘えび・白がすえび・しまえび
items.en: Local raw shrimp — sweet shrimp, gasu-ebi, striped shrimp
items.note: Gasu-ebi is the one to notice: too fragile to ship, so it is eaten almost only in Ishikawa, and sweeter than ama-ebi.

items.en: Evening kaiseki, eleven courses
items.note: Sakizuke opener, appetiser, clear soup, sashimi, grilled, simmered, vinegared, the rice course, a closing miso soup, pickles and dessert; ¥28,000 and ¥32,000 versions exist, and the price already includes tax, service and the room charge.

items.en: Lunch kaiseki, ten courses
items.note: Appetiser, sashimi, grilled, steamed, simmered, rice, closing soup, pickles and dessert — the cheapest way into a Kaga-cuisine ryotei that charges ¥25,000 at night; ¥15,000, ¥18,000 and ¥22,000 tiers too.

items.en: Light lunch set, eight items (four people minimum)
items.note: Aperitif, a kuchitori assortment, sashimi, a steamed dish, rice, closing soup, pickles and dessert; quoted before tax, but the room charge is waived.

items.en: Grilled-eel lunch box, to take away
items.note: Eel dipped in the head chef's tare and laid over scrambled egg, on rice mixed with chopped pickled ginger, with sweet-vinegared lotus root and ginger — the tare is soy sauce and mirin, so wheat.

items.en: Wagyu sirloin steak lunch box
items.note: Sirloin packed edge to edge with grilled aubergine, courgette, lotus root, broccoli and tomato, tamagoyaki and rice; the steak sauce is soy-based.

items.en: Scattered-sashimi sushi box (15 Oct – 30 Apr only)
items.note: Tuna, salmon, eel, scallop, sweet shrimp and cured mackerel dipped in the chef's cut soy sauce over red-vinegar sushi rice, finished with edible gold leaf — the gold is inert, the soy sauce is not.

items.en: Four-compartment lacquer lunch box, built to your budget
items.note: The classic cross-partitioned box used for meetings and formal lunches; you name the budget and the kitchen fills it.

items.en: Two-tier lunch box
items.note: Quoted before tax; boxes need three days' notice by fax and a minimum order of several units, and box sales pause June–September.

items.ja: ご結納・両家お顔合わせのお食事
items.en: Betrothal / family-introduction meal
items.note: A ryotei this old does much of its trade in engagement and celebration meals, served in detached rooms that seat one to twenty.

items.en: Post-memorial-service meal
items.note: Booked after Buddhist memorial rites; the same detached rooms, a quieter menu.

items.en: Fukui-style soba: cold buckwheat noodles under grated daikon with cold dashi poured over
items.note: The house style — Echizen (Fukui) soba, eaten cold with pungent grated daikon in the dashi.

items.en: Oroshi soba lunch set with a small inari sushi and a side dish
items.note: The set adds a small sweet-tofu-pouch sushi and a kobachi side; both carry soy sauce.

items.ja: 油揚げ入りおろしそば
items.en: Oroshi soba with a thick slab of grilled fried tofu
items.note: Diners describe a thick Tochio-style abura-age rather than a thin sheet.

items.en: Soba topped with a sweet-simmered herring fillet
items.note: Soy-and-sugar simmered herring; noodles are wheat-blended.

items.en: Wheat-gluten cuisine course — the three tier
items.note: A whole kaiseki lunch built on fu, eaten looking onto the garden; book by the previous day, because the dining room opens only on reserved days.

items.en: Wheat-gluten cuisine course — the four tier
items.note: More dishes, same principle: fu is the protein throughout, which makes it one of the few near-meatless kaiseki meals in Japan and 100% off-limits to coeliacs.

items.en: Wheat-gluten cuisine course — the five tier
items.note: The full course; dashi is still bonito unless arranged otherwise, so vegetarian-leaning rather than vegan.

items.en: Fu — wheat gluten, the thing this entire shop is made of
items.note: Per the shop: wheat flour is kneaded with salt and water, rested, then washed over and over until only the protein is left. That protein is gluten, and it is the whole product; the white water washed off becomes starch.

items.en: Fresh fu — soft, springy, cut into blocks
items.note: Domestic wheat gluten kneaded with glutinous-rice flour, then steamed, boiled or simmered; chewy like mochi and usually served in a simmered dish.

items.en: Sudare-fu — the flat comb-marked slab that goes into jibuni
items.note: Kaga's own fu: gluten kneaded with plain rice flour and pressed against a bamboo blind, which leaves the ridges. It is the piece floating in every bowl of jibuni.

items.en: Kuruma-fu — the ridged wheel you meet in Kanazawa oden
items.note: Gluten plus wheat flour baked over an open flame in layers around a rod, which gives the wheel its rings; it drinks up broth like a sponge and is a defining item of Kanazawa oden.

items.en: Soup fu — small dried pieces for miso soup
items.note: Baked flat on iron rather than over flame; the coloured ones use only natural pigments, per the shop.

items.en: Fu manju — sweet bean paste wrapped in fresh gluten
items.note: A cool, slippery summer sweet: lightly sweetened bean paste wrapped in nama-fu. Wheat gluten again, so no part of it is gluten-free.

items.en: Oyaki — chunky bean paste in fresh gluten, griddled
items.note: Domestic tsubu-an wrapped in nama-fu and baked; nothing like the Nagano vegetable oyaki that shares the name.

items.en: Fu karinto — sugar-glazed crunchy gluten sticks
items.note: Baked fu fried and coated in sugar; the standard souvenir from this shop and, again, pure wheat.

kz_le_mars.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The à la carte page prices are tax-included; the older Les Plats / Les Desserts pages list prices before tax. A per-person table charge of ¥660 applies.

items.en: Lunch course — starter, a main you choose from 3–4, bread, drink and dessert
items.note: Served 12:00–13:30 (last order); no lunch on Thursdays, and à la carte is only taken until 13:00.

items.en: Dinner tasting course, three price tiers
items.note: Content is agreed when you book, so this is where to raise allergies; must be reserved by the previous day.

items.ja: 本日のシャルキュトリー
items.en: Charcuterie of the day — house-cured pork and terrines
items.note: The heart of this bistro; what is ready changes daily, so look at the board.

items.ja: パテ・ド・カンパーニュ
items.en: Pâté de campagne — coarse country pork pâté
items.note: Part of the daily charcuterie; country pâtés sometimes carry breadcrumb or flour as a binder, so ask.

items.ja: 豚足・豚耳・タンのテリーヌ
items.en: Terrine of pig's trotter, ear and tongue
items.note: Set in its own natural gelatine — the sort of nose-to-tail plate this place exists for.

items.en: Pork rillettes — shredded pork potted in its own fat
items.note: Spread it on the bread; pork and fat only, but it arrives with wheat bread.

items.en: Jambon blanc — house-made boiled ham
items.note: Made in house; cured meats can carry wheat-derived seasonings, so confirm.

items.ja: シャルキュトリー盛り合わせ
items.en: Charcuterie assortment — 3 or 5 kinds
items.note: The best way to taste the range; choices can include beef-tripe terrine, chicken-liver mousse, jambon persillé and smoked ham.

items.ja: オニオンスープグラタン
items.en: French onion soup gratinée
items.note: Bread and melted cheese are baked on top, and the broth is beef stock.

items.ja: フランス産エスカルゴのオーブン焼き
items.en: French snails baked in garlic-parsley butter
items.note: Snail, butter, garlic and parsley — usually gluten-free in itself, but breadcrumbs are a common addition, so ask.

items.en: Œuf mayonnaise — halved boiled egg under mayonnaise
items.note: The cheapest thing on the list and a French bistro standard; egg, oil and mustard.

items.en: Crudités — a spread of raw and dressed vegetable salads
items.note: The nearest thing to a vegetable main here, but the individual salads often use mayonnaise — ask which ones.

items.ja: アルザス風シュークルート
items.en: Choucroute alsacienne — pork and sausages braised with sauerkraut
items.note: One of the two dishes the owner says the restaurant is for; the sausages are the wheat risk (rusk fillers), so ask.

items.en: Cassoulet — duck leg, sausage and white haricot beans slow-baked together
items.note: Traditional cassoulet is finished with a breadcrumb crust and the sausage may contain wheat — ask before assuming.

items.en: Andouillette — the pungent French tripe-and-offal sausage
items.note: Made in house. Powerfully offal-y and an acquired taste even in France — order it knowing that.

items.en: Boudin noir — French blood sausage
items.note: Blood sausages very often contain breadcrumbs or flour; ask.

items.en: Petit salé — lightly salt-cured Noto pork, simmered
items.note: Made with pork from the Noto peninsula north of Kanazawa; usually served with lentils.

items.en: Confit de canard — duck leg cooked and preserved in its own fat, then crisped
items.note: Duck, salt and fat — one of the more likely gluten-free mains here, but confirm the garnish and sauce.

items.ja: マグレ・ド・カナール（鴨胸肉）のロティ
items.en: Roast magret — the breast of a fattened duck, served pink
items.note: The most expensive plate on the standing list; the sauce is where any flour would be.

items.ja: 国産牛ほほ肉のブイヨン煮
items.en: Japanese beef cheek simmered about seven hours with vegetables, pot-au-feu style
items.note: Listed as a take-away main option; if it is on the blackboard in the restaurant, it is worth asking for.

items.en: Crème brûlée
items.note: Cream, egg yolk, sugar — no flour, but plenty of dairy.

items.ja: アルマニャック風味のガトーショコラ
items.en: Chocolate cake scented with Armagnac brandy
items.note: Some gâteaux au chocolat use almost no flour and some use plenty — ask this kitchen which.

items.ja: 果物のアルマニャック風味
items.en: Fruit steeped in Armagnac
items.note: Fruit and brandy — potentially the one dessert here that suits both diets; confirm nothing is served with it.

items.en: Caramelised banana
items.note: Cooked in butter and sugar, usually with ice cream alongside.

items.ja: 季節のフルーツのタルト
items.en: Seasonal fruit tart
items.note: Made by the in-house pastry chef; pastry base means wheat and butter.

items.ja: カヌレ・ド・ボルドー
items.en: Canelé de Bordeaux — small dark caramelised custard cake
items.note: A local cult item — reserve at least four days ahead and a minimum of five; flour, egg and milk.

items.en: Plain cabbage okonomiyaki — batter and cabbage only
items.note: Okonomiyaki batter is wheat flour and the finishing sauce contains wheat, so nothing here is GF.

items.en: Pork okonomiyaki
items.note: Thin pork belly laid over the cabbage batter.

items.en: Pork okonomiyaki with an egg
items.note: Egg is an add-on, not standard.

items.en: Squid okonomiyaki
items.note: Chopped squid in the batter.

items.en: Squid okonomiyaki with an egg
items.note: Same with an egg cracked on.

items.en: Mixed okonomiyaki — pork and squid
items.note: The usual order if you want both.

items.en: Mixed pork-and-squid okonomiyaki with an egg
items.note: Still under ¥400 — this is an old-fashioned neighbourhood price list.

items.en: Beef-tendon okonomiyaki
items.note: Slow-cooked beef tendon, the richest option on the griddle.

items.en: Pork yakisoba — fried wheat noodles with pork and cabbage
items.note: Yakisoba noodles are wheat and the brown sauce contains wheat too.

items.en: Half portion of pork yakisoba
items.note: Half sizes exist for most of the yakisoba — handy if you want to try two things.

items.en: Pork yakisoba seasoned with salt instead of brown sauce
items.note: Lighter than the sauce version, but the noodles are still wheat.

items.en: Squid yakisoba
items.note: Squid instead of pork.

items.en: Half portion of squid yakisoba
items.note: Half size.

items.en: Squid yakisoba seasoned with salt
items.note: Salt-seasoned, no brown sauce.

items.en: Mixed pork-and-squid yakisoba
items.note: Both proteins.

items.en: Half portion of mixed yakisoba
items.note: Half size.

items.en: Pad-Thai-style yakisoba — the shop's noodles with Thai seasoning
items.note: A surprise on a Showa-era dagashi-shop griddle; still the shop's wheat yakisoba noodle.

items.en: Curry yakisoba, made with Champion Curry's roux
items.note: Uses roux from Champion Curry, the Kanazawa curry chain; the roux is flour-based.

items.en: Yakisoba chopped and fried together with rice
items.note: Noodles and rice on the same griddle — a Kobe idea that travelled.

items.en: Large portion (surcharge)
items.note: Add-on to any yakisoba.

items.en: Add a fried egg on top
items.note: Add-on.

items.en: Takoyaki, 6 pieces — batter balls with octopus
items.note: Wheat-flour batter, octopus inside, wheat-containing sauce on top.

items.en: Takoyaki, 10 pieces
items.note: The bigger box.

items.en: 'Kado balls' — 6 takoyaki-shaped balls filled with sweet red bean paste
items.note: The shop's own sweet twist on takoyaki; wheat batter, so not GF.

items.en: Grilled loach glazed kabayaki-style (summer only)
items.note: A genuinely old-Kanazawa summer snack; the glaze is soy-sauce based.

items.en: Smack — a Hokuriku regional bottled soft drink
items.note: A local nostalgia drink you will not find outside the region; ask whether it contains dairy.

items.en: Ramune — marble-stoppered lemon-lime soda
items.note: Push the marble down with the plunger in the cap.

items.ja: ホッピーセット（白・黒）
items.en: Hoppy set — a bottle of near-alcohol-free malt drink plus a glass of shochu to mix, white or black
items.note: Hoppy itself is a malted-barley beverage — not gluten-free.

items.en: Chilled sake served in a wooden masu box
items.note: Rice and koji only; the cedar box adds its own scent.

items.en: Paper cup — what you buy in order to drink your bottle standing at the counter
items.note: This is how the kakuuchi here works: pick a bottle off the shelf, pay for it plus ten yen for a cup, drink it on the spot. There is no separate by-the-glass list and no kitchen — people carry crab or sashimi in from the Omicho stalls outside.

items.en: Cloudy unfiltered sake, sweet and thick with rice sediment — 300ml bottle
items.note: The staff pick for a first-timer and small enough to finish standing up; sake is rice, koji and water, with no wheat and nothing animal.

items.ja: 天狗舞 山廃仕込純米酒
items.en: Kanazawa's most famous house style: yamahai junmai, deep and slightly gamey
items.note: Yamahai means the starter soured naturally, which gives Tengumai its heavy, almost cheesy character. Lower price is 720ml, higher is the 1.8L.

items.ja: 天狗舞 純米酒 旨醇 1.8L
items.en: Dry everyday junmai in a full 1.8-litre bottle
items.note: The table-sake grade of Tengumai; you will meet it on izakaya lists all over Kanazawa.

items.ja: 天狗舞 金沢酵母大吟醸 720ml
items.en: Daiginjo brewed with the local Kanazawa yeast strain
items.note: Kanazawa yeast is prized for clean floral aroma — worth tasting beside the yamahai to see how far one brewery's range stretches.

items.ja: 天狗舞 次郎冠者 720ml 箱入り
items.en: Boxed 720ml bottle, the common gift choice
items.note: Comes boxed, so it travels; the shop wraps for gifts.

items.ja: 天狗舞 古古酒純米大吟醸（箱入）
items.en: Long-aged junmai daiginjo, amber and sherry-like
items.note: Aged sake is a different drink entirely — nutty and oxidative rather than fruity.

items.ja: 手取川 名流純米酒 大辛口
items.en: Bone-dry junmai from Shirayama, clean and sharp
items.note: Okarakuchi means very dry; a good foil for the oily local fish.

items.en: Polished junmai ginjo, softer and more aromatic
items.note: Tedorigawa is the river that waters the Kaga plain; the brewery sits on it.

items.ja: 手取川 あらばしり大吟醸生酒
items.en: Unpasteurised free-run daiginjo — the first, cloudiest part of the press
items.note: Nama sake needs refrigeration; not the bottle to carry round all day in summer.

items.ja: 手取川 瑞流 純米大吟醸（化粧箱入）
items.en: Top-end junmai daiginjo in a presentation box
items.note: The shop's flagship Tedorigawa gift bottle.

items.ja: 農口尚彦研究所 観音下
items.en: Sake from the institute built around Noguchi Naohiko, the living-legend brewmaster
items.section: 日本酒 農口尚彦研究所
items.note: Noguchi is called the god of toji; the institute exists to record his technique. Good warmed as well as chilled.

items.ja: 農口尚彦研究所 夏の生酒 無濾過生
items.romaji: Noguchi Naohiko Natsu no Nama-shu Muroka Nama
items.en: Summer-release sake, neither charcoal-filtered nor pasteurised
items.section: 日本酒 農口尚彦研究所
items.note: Muroka nama is seasonal and short-lived — buy it to drink, not to carry home.

items.ja: 加賀鳶 純米大吟醸 藍
items.en: Bright, brisk junmai daiginjo from Fukumitsuya in Kanazawa city
items.note: Kagatobi is named after the Kaga clan's firefighters; Fukumitsuya is the oldest brewery in Ishikawa.

items.ja: 常きげん 山廃仕込 山純
items.en: Yamahai junmai from Kaga, robust and food-friendly
items.note: Another yamahai house — worth comparing directly against the Tengumai.

items.ja: 常きげん 純米吟醸 風神
items.en: "Wind god" junmai ginjo
items.note: Sold as a pair with the 雷神 (thunder god) ginjo.

items.ja: 梵 純米55 特別限定純米酒
items.en: Fukui's Born, rice polished to 55 percent
items.note: Filed under 県外 (out-of-prefecture) — the shelves here are otherwise almost entirely Ishikawa.

items.ja: 満寿泉 純米大吟醸 720ml（箱入り）
items.en: Toyama's Masuizumi, boxed
items.note: From neighbouring Toyama; a classic match for white shrimp and firefly squid.

items.ja: ひゃくまん丸大豆醤油
items.en: Ishikawa whole-soybean soy sauce, sold as a souvenir
items.note: Ordinary koikuchi soy sauce is brewed from wheat as well as soybeans, so this is not a gluten-free souvenir.

items.en: Beef tongue, cut thick — crunchy, and it goes tough if you overcook it
items.note: The priciest thing on the grill list. Ask whether it comes shio (salt) or tare; the tare is soy-based and therefore wheat.

items.en: Pork large intestine — soft, fatty, the shop's signature cheap cut
items.note: Served in a heap big enough that diners ask whether it is really one portion. It arrives pre-marinated in tare, so wheat.

items.en: Cheek meat — fibrous but melting
items.note: Comes marinated in the house tare.

items.en: Pork belly, heavily marbled; the fat turns sweet on the grill
items.note: Reviewers rate this the best thing in the shop. Tare-marinated.

items.en: Beef short rib / belly, generous portion
items.note: Tare-marinated, like almost everything on the grill here.

items.en: Pork loin
items.note: Tare-marinated.

items.en: Liver — reviewers single this out as unusually fresh, cut with sharp corners
items.note: Tare-marinated; no off-smell reported, which is the test for a horumon shop.

items.en: Cartilage — all crunch
items.note: Tare-marinated.

items.en: Heart — springy and clean-tasting
items.note: Tare-marinated.

items.en: Grilled mackerel — yes, a grill-your-own yakiniku counter also does fish
items.note: The regulars order the grilled fish. Salt-grilled fish is one of the safer things here, but it shares the grill with tare-soaked offal.

items.en: Grilled Pacific saury, autumn's cheap luxury
items.note: Usually salted only; the shared grill is the risk.

items.en: Grilled salted salmon
items.note: Salt-cured, no sauce — again the shared grill is the issue.

items.en: Grilled yellowtail, the Hokuriku winter fish
items.note: Buri from the Sea of Japan is what Kanazawa eats in December; confirm it is not teriyaki-glazed.

items.en: Grilled squid
items.note: Usually brushed with soy at the end — ask for it plain.

items.en: Grilled prawns
items.note: Shell-on and salted.

items.en: Clams cooked on the grill in their shells
items.note: Often finished with butter and a splash of soy.

items.en: Thick deep-fried tofu, reheated on the grill
items.note: Tofu itself is fine, but it is normally eaten with soy sauce and bonito flakes.

items.en: Fried wheat noodles — the shop advertises it on the wall as the way to finish
items.note: Wheat noodles plus a soy-and-fruit sauce; wheat twice over.

items.en: Stir-fried vegetables
items.note: Seasoned with soy sauce; often has pork in it, so ask.

items.en: Potato croquette, breadcrumbed and fried
items.note: Panko crumb — wheat.

items.en: Plain white rice
items.note: Unseasoned steamed rice is the one genuinely wheat-free plate in the shop — watch the shared scoop.

items.en: Miso soup
items.note: Miso can be barley-based and the stock is bonito.

items.en: Kimchi
items.note: Commercial kimchi commonly contains fish sauce or salted shrimp, and sometimes wheat starch.

items.en: Pickled daikon
items.note: Japanese pickles are often sweetened with a soy-containing seasoning liquid.

items.en: Spinach, blanched
items.note: Ohitashi-style spinach is normally steeped in bonito dashi and soy.

items.en: Pan-fried gyoza — 7 small one-bite dumplings, crisp-bottomed
items.note: Wrappers are wheat and the vinegar-soy dip is wheat soy sauce; a reviewer counted seven per plate.

items.en: The house gyoza — the shop's own signature filling
items.note: The name dish; reviewers note a herby, coriander-ish note in the filling.

items.en: Stick gyoza — long cigar-shaped dumplings
items.note: Rolled long rather than pleated, so more crisp surface per bite.

items.en: Gyoza made with chicken skin
items.note: Still served with the usual wheat-soy dip.

items.en: 'Kanazawa gyoza' — the local-style version
items.note: One of roughly eight gyoza varieties on the board.

items.en: Gyoza filled with spicy cod roe and perilla leaf
items.note: Mentaiko is cured pollock roe, usually seasoned with soy and sake.

items.en: Coriander gyoza
items.note: For the coriander crowd; ask if you want it left out.

items.en: 'Paku-cheese' gyoza — coriander plus cheese
items.note: A pun on pakuchi (coriander) and cheese. Contains dairy.

items.en: Steamed dumplings
items.note: Steamed rather than fried; the wrapper is still wheat.

items.en: Thin pan-fried Chinese flatbread, chewy, eaten with ponzu
items.note: Taiwanese-style bing; a wheat-flour pancake, and the ponzu contains soy sauce.

items.en: Deep-fried takoyaki — crisp outside, molten inside
items.note: Wheat batter, deep-fried; a visiting Osakan rated it highly.

items.en: Cucumber with salami
items.note: Described as tasting like a sandwich with the bread removed; confirm the salami has no wheat filler.

items.en: Soy-simmered soft-boiled egg
items.note: Jammy yolk; the simmering liquid is wheat-based soy sauce.

items.en: Cod-roe and potato salad
items.note: Mashed potato bound with cod roe and mayonnaise — contains egg and fish.

items.en: Beef-tendon croquette
items.note: Panko crumb and a flour dusting.

items.en: Chicken nanban — battered fried chicken in sweet vinegar with tartare (half portion available)
items.note: Flour-and-egg batter, then a sweet soy-vinegar glaze.

items.ja: 炒めもやし肉あんかけ
items.en: Stir-fried bean sprouts and pork under a thick starchy sauce
items.note: Starch-thickened but soy-seasoned.

items.en: Numbing-spicy edamame — Sichuan pepper and chilli
items.note: 'Shibi' is the numbing tingle of Sichuan pepper; confirm the seasoning has no soy sauce.

items.en: Sapporo draught beer
items.note: Cheap draught — this is a standing bar, so the beer is the anchor price.

items.en: Bottled beer, medium bottle
items.note: Barley malt; not gluten-free.

items.en: Lemon sour — shochu, soda and lemon
items.note: Shochu can be distilled from barley; ask if you are strict about distilled grain.

items.en: Suntory 'Sui' gin with soda
items.note: Grain-distilled gin with yuzu, green tea and ginger botanicals.

items.en: Premium beef tongue, salt-seasoned only
items.note: A sign behind the counter says the shop seasons with Suzu no shio, the sea salt from the tip of the Noto peninsula that high-end ryotei use — so the shio cuts really are salt-only, but confirm nothing else is brushed on.

items.en: Wagyu sirloin, sliced for the grill
items.note: Ask for shio rather than tare if wheat matters; tare is a soy-sauce marinade.

items.en: Skirt / outside diaphragm — technically offal but eats like steak
items.note: The everyday favourite cut in a Japanese yakiniku shop. Shio or tare, so ask.

items.en: Premium pork large intestine, fatty and chewy
items.note: Horumon is normally sold pre-soaked in tare; assume soy sauce.

items.en: Short rib, the standard yakiniku cut
items.note: Reported as part of a shiro / wagyu / karubi combination plate around ¥1,480; the karubi comes tare-marinated.

items.en: Kimchi mixed with fermented soybeans, topped with shredded nori and spring onion
items.note: An unusual pairing worth trying. Natto's sauce sachet is soy-sauce based, and shop kimchi often contains fish, so neither flag is clean.

items.en: Scallop adductor, grilled
items.note: The counter sign specifically recommends eating this with the Suzu salt rather than sauce.

items.en: Pig's trotter, grilled
items.note: Gelatinous rather than meaty; usually eaten with salt and citrus.

items.en: Green salad, the standard palate-cleaner between grilled cuts
items.note: Japanese house dressings almost always contain soy sauce.

items.en: Kirin Lager, medium bottle
items.note: Barley beer.

items.en: Shochu with soda and lemon
items.note: If the base is imo or kome shochu it is grain-free, but mugi (barley) shochu is common — ask which.
